# `silk/time/calendar`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Dates in other calendars than ISO 8601: [`Calendar`](#Calendar), [`CalendarDate`](#CalendarDate), [`Era`](#Era), and
[`MonthCode`](#MonthCode).

## When to use

Use [`CalendarDate`](#CalendarDate) to show a day to a person who reads another calendar, to read a date that
a person gives in one, and to count years and months as that calendar counts them. For the
dates that programs store and exchange, use `PlainDate` of `silk.time.plain_date`.

## Details

A [`CalendarDate`](#CalendarDate) is a `PlainDate` seen in one of 16 calendars. [`CalendarDate.of`](#CalendarDate.impl.of) converts a
`PlainDate`, and [`CalendarDate.date`](#CalendarDate.impl.date) gives it back. The text form is the ISO 8601 date with
the calendar in an annotation, as in `2026-11-19[u-ca=hebrew]`, which is the form of RFC 9557
and of ECMAScript Temporal.

The fields and the arithmetic follow ECMAScript Temporal:

- [`CalendarDate.year`](#CalendarDate.impl.year) is one count through all eras, and [`CalendarDate.era`](#CalendarDate.impl.era) and
  [`CalendarDate.eraYear`](#CalendarDate.impl.eraYear) give the year as people write it.
- [`CalendarDate.month`](#CalendarDate.impl.month) is the number of the month in its year. [`CalendarDate.monthCode`](#CalendarDate.impl.monthCode) is
  the name of the month that does not change when a year has a leap month.
- [`CalendarDate.checkedAdd`](#CalendarDate.impl.checkedAdd) and [`CalendarDate.until`](#CalendarDate.impl.until) count the years and the months of the
  calendar.

The Hebrew calendar, the Islamic calendars by rule, and the Coptic, Ethiopic, Indian, and
Persian calendars are computed for every date of `PlainDate`. The Persian calendar follows the
33-year rule with the corrections of Unicode ICU, which keep it on the astronomical calendar of
Iran. The Umm al-Qura calendar has a table for the years 1300 to 1600 of the Hijra, and the
Chinese and Dangi calendars have tables for 1800 to 2200; they are in
`silk.time.calendar_data`.

## Gotchas

The Chinese and Dangi calendars have no data outside 1800-01-25 to 2201-02-03. A date outside
gives `CalendarError.OutOfRange`.

The Japanese calendar has the eras from Meiji on, and Meiji starts on 1873-01-01, the day
Japan took the Gregorian calendar. Earlier dates have the eras `ce` and `bce`.

## Examples

### Show a date in the Hebrew calendar

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.calendar { Calendar, CalendarDate, CalendarError }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return match CalendarDate.of(Calendar.Hebrew, PlainDate.make(2026, 11, 19)) {
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Success { value } => {
      // 9 Kislev 5787. Kislev is the third month.
      if value.year() != 5787 || value.month() != 3 || value.day() != 9 {
        return 1
      }
      if value.monthCode().number != 3 || value.monthCode().leap {
        return 2
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Failure {..} => 3
  }
}
```

### Read a date that a person gives in the Japanese calendar

```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.calendar { Calendar, CalendarDate, CalendarError, Era }
import silk.time.period { Overflow }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // Reiwa 8, month 11, day 19.
  let year = match Calendar.Japanese.yearOfEra(Era.Reiwa, 8) {
    Option<i32>.Some { value } => value
    Option<i32>.None => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  return match CalendarDate.fromFields(Calendar.Japanese, year, 11, 19, Overflow.Reject) {
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Success { value } => {
      let date = value.date()
      let expected = PlainDate.make(2026, 11, 19)
      if &date != &expected {
        return 2
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Failure {..} => 3
  }
}
```

### Add a year in a calendar with leap months

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.calendar { Calendar, CalendarDate, CalendarError, MonthCode }
import silk.time.period { Overflow, Period }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // 30 Adar I 5784. The year 5785 has no Adar I, so one year later is in Adar.
  let start = match CalendarDate.fromMonthCode(Calendar.Hebrew, 5784, MonthCode.make(5, true), 30, Overflow.Reject) {
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Failure {..} => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  return match start.checkedAdd(Period.ofYears(1), Overflow.Constrain) {
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Success { value } => {
      // Adar has 29 days.
      if value.monthCode().number != 6 || value.day() != 29 {
        return 2
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>.Failure {..} => 3
  }
}
```

A calendar: a way to name a day with a year, a month, and a day of the month.

### Details

The names are the calendar identifiers of Unicode CLDR, which ECMAScript Temporal and the
`[u-ca=...]` annotation of RFC 9557 use.

<a id="MonthCode"></a>

## `MonthCode`

```silk
pub struct MonthCode
```

The name of a month that is the same in every year, such as `M05` or `M05L`.

### Details

In a calendar with leap months, the number of a month in the year changes: the Hebrew month
Nisan is month 7 of a common year and month 8 of a leap year. The month code does not change:
Nisan is always `M07`. A leap month has the number of the month before it and the letter `L`.
In the Hebrew calendar the only leap month is `M05L`, Adar I. In the Chinese and Dangi
calendars a leap month can follow any month.

<a id="MonthCode.number"></a>

### Field `number`

```silk
pub number: u8
```

The number in the code, from 1.

<a id="MonthCode.leap"></a>

### Field `leap`

```silk
pub leap: bool
```

`true` for a leap month, written with `L`.

<a id="CalendarDate"></a>

## `CalendarDate`

```silk
pub struct CalendarDate
```

A day in one calendar.

### Details

A `CalendarDate` holds a `PlainDate` and a [`Calendar`](#Calendar). The year, the month, and the day are
the fields of that day in the calendar. Two values are equal when they name the same day in
the same calendar.

The year is the year that arithmetic uses. It can be zero or negative. Calendars with eras also
give an [`Era`](#Era) and a year of the era, which is what people write.

<a id="Calendar.impl.yearOfEra"></a>

### Method `yearOfEra`

```silk
pub fn yearOfEra(self: Self, era: Era, eraYear: i32) -> Option<i32>
```

Returns the year that `eraYear` of `era` is in the calendar, or `None` when `era` is not an
era of the calendar.

#### Details

The result is the year that [`CalendarDate.year`](#CalendarDate.impl.year) returns and [`CalendarDate.fromFields`](#CalendarDate.impl.fromFields)
takes. Year 1 of an era that counts back, such as `bce`, is year 0.

`ad` and `bc` are not separate eras: use `Era.Ce` and `Era.Bce`.

<a id="Calendar.impl.monthDayReference"></a>

### Method `monthDayReference`

```silk
pub fn monthDayReference(self: Self, code: MonthCode, day: u8, overflow: Overflow) -> Option<PlainDate>
```

Returns the ISO 8601 date that stands for a month and a day of the calendar without a year,
or `None` when no year has that day, or the overflow rule is `Overflow.Reject` and the day
does not exist as given.

#### Details

This is the reference date of an ECMAScript `Temporal.PlainMonthDay`. For the calendars with
the ISO 8601 months it is in 1972. For the others it is the last day with that month code
and day at or before the end of 1972, except a few days that need an earlier or a later
year. With `Overflow.Constrain`, a day past the longest form of the month becomes its last
day, and a leap month that no year has with that day becomes the common month.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl"></a>

## Implementation `CalendarDate`

```silk
impl CalendarDate
```

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.of"></a>

### Associated function `of`

```silk
pub fn of(calendar: Calendar, date: PlainDate) -> Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>
```

Returns `date` in `calendar`.

#### Errors

- `CalendarError.OutOfRange` if the calendar has no data for the date. Only `Chinese` and
  `Dangi` have a limit: 1800-01-25 to 2201-02-03.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.fromFields"></a>

### Associated function `fromFields`

```silk
pub fn fromFields(calendar: Calendar, year: i32, month: u8, day: u8, overflow: Overflow) -> Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>
```

Returns the date with the given year, number of the month in the year, and day of the month.

#### Details

`year` is the year that [`CalendarDate.year`](#CalendarDate.impl.year) returns. For a year of an era, convert it with
[`Calendar.yearOfEra`](#Calendar.impl.yearOfEra) first. `month` counts the months of that year from 1, so in a leap
year of a calendar with leap months it is not the number in the month code.

#### Errors

- `CalendarError.NoSuchMonth` if `month` is 0, or the year has fewer months and `overflow`
  is `Overflow.Reject`. With `Overflow.Constrain` the last month is used.
- `CalendarError.NoSuchDay` if `day` is 0, or the month has fewer days and `overflow` is
  `Overflow.Reject`. With `Overflow.Constrain` the last day is used.
- `CalendarError.OutOfRange` if the date is outside the range of `PlainDate` or the calendar
  has no data for the year.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.fromMonthCode"></a>

### Associated function `fromMonthCode`

```silk
pub fn fromMonthCode(calendar: Calendar, year: i32, code: MonthCode, day: u8, overflow: Overflow) -> Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>
```

Returns the date with the given year, month code, and day of the month.

#### Details

With `Overflow.Constrain`, a leap month in a year without it becomes the month that takes
its place: Adar (`M06`) for the Hebrew `M05L`, and the month with the same number for a
Chinese or Dangi leap month.

#### Errors

- `CalendarError.NoSuchMonth` if no year of the calendar has a month with that code, or
  this year does not have it and `overflow` is `Overflow.Reject`.
- `CalendarError.NoSuchDay` if `day` is 0, or the month has fewer days and `overflow` is
  `Overflow.Reject`.
- `CalendarError.OutOfRange` if the date is outside the range of `PlainDate` or the calendar
  has no data for the year.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.year"></a>

### Method `year`

```silk
pub fn year(self: Self) -> i32
```

Returns the year, counted on one line through all eras. It can be zero or negative.

#### Details

It is the year of the main era of the calendar where that era applies: the ISO 8601 year for
`gregory` and `japanese`, the year of the Hijra for the Islamic calendars. For `chinese` and
`dangi`, which do not number their years, it is the ISO 8601 year in which the year starts.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.checkedAdd"></a>

### Method `checkedAdd`

```silk
pub fn checkedAdd(self: Self, period: Period, overflow: Overflow) -> Result<CalendarDate, CalendarError>
```

Returns the date that `period` leads to from this date, counted in the calendar.

#### Details

The years are added first and keep the month code: one year after Nisan is Nisan. Then the
months are added by counting months of the calendar through the years. If the month reached
has no such day, `Overflow.Constrain` uses its last day. Then the weeks and the days are
added, with the whole days of the time part of the period. This is the rule of ECMAScript
Temporal.

With `Overflow.Constrain`, a leap month that the year reached does not have becomes the
month that takes its place, as in [`CalendarDate.fromMonthCode`](#CalendarDate.impl.fromMonthCode).

#### Errors

- `CalendarError.NoSuchMonth` or `NoSuchDay` if `overflow` is `Overflow.Reject` and the
  month or the day does not exist in the year or the month reached.
- `CalendarError.OutOfRange` if the result is outside the range of `PlainDate` or the
  calendar has no data for it.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.until"></a>

### Method `until`

```silk
pub fn until(self: Self, other: CalendarDate, largest: DateUnit) -> Result<Period, CalendarError>
```

Returns the span from this date to `other`, counted in the calendar in `largest` units
first. It is negative when `other` is earlier, and its time part is empty.

#### Details

With `DateUnit.Year`, the result has the most whole years that can be added to this date
without passing `other`, then the most whole months, then the days that are left. With
`DateUnit.Month` it has months and days, with `DateUnit.Week` weeks and days, and with
`DateUnit.Day` only days. Adding the result to this date with [`CalendarDate.checkedAdd`](#CalendarDate.impl.checkedAdd)
gives `other`. This is the rule of ECMAScript Temporal.

#### Errors

- `CalendarError.CalendarMismatch` if `other` is in another calendar. Convert one of the
  dates with [`CalendarDate.withCalendar`](#CalendarDate.impl.withCalendar) first.

<a id="CalendarDate.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<CalendarDate, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a date with a calendar annotation, such as `2026-11-19[u-ca=hebrew]`.

#### Details

The text is the one that `PlainDate.parse` reads: the date is always written in the ISO 8601
calendar, and the annotation names the calendar of the result. A text without a calendar
annotation gives a date in `Calendar.Iso8601`.

#### Errors

- The errors of `PlainDate.parse` for the date.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if the annotation names no calendar of
  [`Calendar`](#Calendar).
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the calendar has no data for the date.
